# Roof racks and storage

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Bolt a camo tarp to steel rails using exhaust clamps, then attach a custom PVC frame. [t1692]

Attach and tie off a tarp onto roof rack rails using grommets. [t1692]

[Partial] Attach a Thule cargo box to the roof rack bars, then load approximately 80 pounds of gear. [t1484]

Identify the rubber trim piece attached to the front fairing, then remove the entire assembly as one single unit. [t1808]

Inspect rear roof supports to see if they are still attached to the headliner. [t1458]

## Procedure

1. Inspect the rear roof supports to see if they are still attached to the headliner.

_Procedure reported by [t1458]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/roof-supports-attn-headliner-diyers.5123/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1484] [Partial]</summary>

1. Cut two pieces of 1-1/2 in. x 14-Gauge zinc-plated slotted angle to a length of 72 inches each.
2. [Partial] Cut five pieces of 1/2 in. electric metallic tube conduit, with three cross bars cut from the first piece and one bar remaining on each of the other two pieces.
3. Drill out four fender washers per cross bar location to fit the rivets inside the slotted angle iron.
4. Attach the angled side rails to the stock roof rails using 5/16 in. #18 x 1 inch hex bolts and nylock nuts through the Nilight mounting brackets.
5. Position a conduit piece between each pair of angle iron cross bars, ensuring three fit per 10 ft length where possible.
6. [Partial] Secure the first end of each conduit to its corresponding slotted angle using two EMT straps with aluminum rivets on one side.
7. Flip the assembly over and secure the opposite ends of all five conduits to their respective angles using more EMT straps and aluminum rivets.
8. [Partial] Install a 1/8 in. x 3/16 in. aluminum finishing washer under each exposed head of the six rivets per cross bar location for a flush finish.
9. Prime the entire assembled roof rack structure with primer coat paint.
10. [Partial] Apply two coats of topcoat paint over the primed surface to complete the fabrication.
11. Mount the driver-side assembly onto the vehicle's stock rails by attaching the Nilight brackets and bolting them in place.
12. [Partial] Rotate the passenger-side mounting brackets slightly inward until they sit at a 90-degree angle relative to the rack frame.
13. Attach the passenger-side assembly to the vehicle using bolts through the adjusted brackets.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1692] [Partial]</summary>

1. Take the exhaust clamps and place them on the roof rack.
2. Put the back side of each clamp onto the rail first.
3. Add the steel rail to the front of the clamps.
4. Tighten down the nuts securing the rails.
5. Chop off the extra bolt from one of the clamps.
6. Bolt the tarp to the rail in 7 places using leftover hardware.
7. [Partial] Cut a piece of PVC pipe that is exactly 6' long.
8. [Partial] Zip tie the cut piece of PVC to the side of the tarp.
9. Attach two 90* elbows to the main length of PVC pipe.
10. Cut two lengths of pipe for legs, each measuring 6'5" long.
11. [Partial] Connect the leg pieces to the elbows on the main pipe.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1692] [Partial]</summary>

1. Attach a tarp to the roof rack rails using grommets.
2. Tie off the tarp grommets directly onto the roof rack rails.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1484] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Attach a Thule cargo box to the roof rack bars.
2. Load approximately 80 pounds of gear into the box.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1808] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Identify the rubber trim piece attached to the front fairing.
2. Remove the entire assembly as one single unit.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Chop off the extra bolt on the exhaust clamp to allow rolling up and strapping down the tarp. [t1692]
- [Partial] Use a bungee cord to strap down the tarp if driving at high speeds. [t1692]
- [Partial] Ensure the awning is tied down securely in windy conditions. [t1692]
- Use vise grips to hold parts steady while crimping rivets. [t1484]
- Expect to lose some aluminum rivets during fabrication and buy extra packs accordingly. [t1484]
- Attach the driver side first, then install the passenger side. [t1484]
- Be prepared to rotate mounting brackets slightly inward if they do not sit at a perfect 90-degree angle initially. [t1484]
- Use fender washers as the rivets are not large enough for holes in slotted angle iron without them. [t1484]
- Add #6 nickel-plated finishing washers to make the final look smoother and flush against the metal. [t1484]
- [Partial] Note that the bottom seal is integrated into this removable cover rather than sitting directly on the roof rails, preventing damage during removal or painting prep. [t1808]
- Note that these supports may have detached from the roof during previous removals or over time. [t1458]
- [Partial] Check for similar loose support issues in other Xterra owners who have removed their headliners before. [t1458]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Rushing the process without realizing the whole front spoiler assembly comes off together. [t1808]
